correctness.rationale: The stable equations force attacker choices across a fixed bipartition, producing binomial(n,k)*(n-k)^k*k^(n-k) maps with a marked size-k extension. Negative h-second derivative and gamma log-convexity yield strict log concavity. Uniform Stirling gives exact Gaussian scale sqrt(n)/4, and a central Gaussian tail bound plus exponential edge bound proves normalization 1/2 and variance n/16. Finite exact all-map and all-subset replay at n<=6 agrees; computation is corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The exact annealed accepted-size histogram and sharp variance n/16 are neither a statement about even functional cycles nor an implication of the cited CLT for component counts. The inspected 2026 argumentation paper deals with extension diversity, not random accepted cardinality. Conditional mapping-cycle results by Yakymiv are explicitly treated as established prior coverage rather than as new findings. An equivalent two-colouring calculation in older literature remains possible.
residual_risks: The marked-cardinality formula is equivalent to a two-coloring size enumerator; an unpublished or older exact enumeration may give equal or stronger coverage.
The general weighted random A-mapping machinery could subsume a close transformation of this polynomial, though displayed formulas weight component numbers rather than colour-class sizes.
The cited 2015 A-mapping paper and 2019 enumeration paper were compared from abstracts only; no whole-document NOT_COVERING claim is made for them.

value.rationale: The complete annealed marked-cardinality profile is a naturally motivated invariant for Dung semantics. Exact finite counts, global strict log-concavity, exact Gaussian width n/16, and average 1/2 establish a quantitative benchmark and expose a significant distinction between counting extensions across all instances and sampling a typical solvable instance. The new quantity is not a minor numeric increment to an existing count and is not simply the known cycle-count CLT.
